summary: Feed s124_double to NDR is degraded: 29.95 Gbps microbursts overload 10 Gbps tool port (299% capacity) and 99.2% of traffic is encrypted exceeding 90% tolerance, leaving NDR blind and dropping traffic.

findings.root_cause: 99.2% of bytes are encrypted (TLS) vs NDR tolerance of 90%. Traffic is not being decrypted before the packet broker forwards to the NDR - no SSL visibility/decryption zone is in path, so broker is forwarding ciphertext.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR requires full payload for detection but receives opaque ciphertext; payload inspection, JA3/JA4, file extraction and IDS signatures fail, drastically reducing detection coverage to metadata only.

recommended_fix.why: Decrypting (or selective TLS 1.2 decryption with key sharing) before the NDR restores payload visibility so NDR analytics can inspect flows; without it NDR is blind despite receiving both directions.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker is bursting 29.95 Gbps in 1ms intervals into a single 10 Gbps NDR port (299% of capacity). Single-tool feed with no load balancing or aggregation shaping causes microburst overload.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR port buffers overflow and drops packets randomly; TCP reassembly fails, flows appear incomplete, alerts are missed and NDR reports gaps. Even with both directions present, analysis is incomplete.

recommended_fix.why: Hash-based load balancing across 3x10G NDR instances/ports (or 2x with burst buffering) keeps per-port utilization <80% and preserves flow symmetry, eliminating drops while maintaining both directions per flow.
